lesson.subject: literacy
lesson.title: Spirit Bird
lesson.subtitle: How one repeated line makes a message impossible to forget

studentTools: Printed lyric sheet AND Listening Booklet, one each per student
Mini-whiteboards and markers for the check
routineIcons: Voices off, fingers at your chest
Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: Write on the board: The chorus makes you feel it. The verse tells you what to do.
Leave space to build one sentence together in the We Do
videos: Xavier Rudd - Spirit Bird (audio), runs 7 min 11 sec: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TmxSxKxBbQE
urls: Lyric sheet is NOT in this pack. Print the lyrics from a licensed source before the lesson.

resources.label: Spirit Bird Listening Booklet
resources.description: Use with the printed lyric sheet. Listening agreement, the repeated line, and the group chorus planner.
resources.title: Spirit Bird Listening Booklet
resources.subtitle: Keep this beside your lyric sheet.

steps: Voices off for the whole song. All seven minutes.
Follow the words on your lyric sheet with your finger.
Some singing will not sound like English. Listen harder, not louder.

blocks.text: One word for how the song feels to you:
Circle any line on your lyric sheet that comes back more than once.
One line that stayed with you:

organiser.right: What it asks us to do or feel

blocks.heading: The chorus makes you feel it. The verse tells you what to do.

blocks.text: Two lines that show why it matters:

steps: Say the repeated line out loud three times.
Does it ask for something, not just describe something?
Could someone remember it after hearing it once?

blocks.tip: Stretch: write a second line that answers your repeated line, the way a verse answers a chorus.

slides.notes: Open the lesson. One line: today we study a song, and we work out how one repeated line makes a message stay with people.

slides.title: For the teacher: read this before you teach
lines: Print the lyrics from a licensed source, one per student. They are not in this pack.
Paste the chorus and one verse into the two slides marked PASTE.
Timing: launch 5, context 7, listen 9, talk 3, I Do 6, We Do 7, check 3, write 12, close 4.
The listening agreement slide is not optional. Set it before you touch play.
Decision points: the fingers check before group writing, then the exit ticket.
Builds on the First Fleet in Term 1, famous Australians in Term 2, and the Goodes film.
Steer the group task to real groups, not jokes. Name examples before they write.
Booklet and lyric sheet stay side by side on every desk.
slides.notes: Teacher-facing. Two jobs before the bell: print the lyric sheet, and paste the lyrics into the two PASTE slides.
Prep slide. Print the lyric sheet and the booklet, one each per student. Open the video link in a browser tab before the lesson so play is one click. Whiteboards out for the fingers check.

notes.answer: open - land taken, people forced off Country, children taken, racism now
beats: POINT to the three lines.
SAY: Three things you have studied. Today they meet in one song.
ASK: What happened to Aboriginal people after 1788?
30 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: land taken, forced off, treated badly
SCAN the room. Listen for land, and for people.
80%+ naming a loss -> next slide.
Less -> ask who was here before the ships, re-ask.
SAY: A musician said all of that in one song. Today we find out how.
trap: treating it as ancient history that is finished.
Fix: name the Goodes film, ask if that felt long ago, student answers.
notes.prep: Low-coupling launch: every student has met at least one of the three. Whole block under 5 minutes.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning how a songwriter uses one repeated line to make a message stay with people.
successCriteria: I can find the line that Xavier Rudd repeats.
I can explain what that repeated line makes us feel.
I can write a repeated line that stands up for a group of people.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: One repeated line. That is the whole lesson.
SAY: Read the three I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one you can do with the lyric sheet in your hand.
The third one you write in your group at the end.
notes.prep: SC1 find the repeated line. SC2 explain what it asks, the exit evidence. SC3 write one.

slides.meaning: The land, water and sky a group of people belong to.
slides.example: Aboriginal people say they belong to Country, not that they own it.
slides.routine: Say it. Then name one place you feel you belong to.

notes.answer: the land, water and sky a group of people belong to
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Country. Look at the capital C. Say it with me.
SAY: Country is not just dirt. It is land, water, sky and story.
People belong to Country. It is not a thing you buy.
ASK: Name one place you feel you belong to.
15 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: a house, a park, a beach, a town
trap: hearing Country as Australia the nation.
Fix: point to the capital C, say it means a people's own place, student repeats it.
notes.prep: The word the song rests on. Taught once here, used on every slide after.

slides.meaning: The line a songwriter repeats so you cannot forget it.
slides.example: Every time the chorus comes back, the refrain comes back too.
slides.routine: Say it three times, the way a chorus does.

notes.answer: the line a songwriter repeats so you cannot forget it
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Refrain. Say it with me. Refrain.
SAY: The refrain is the line that comes back again and again.
A songwriter repeats the line they most want you to keep.
ASK: Name a song where you know one line by heart.
15 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: any song, any line they can sing back
trap: thinking the refrain means the whole chorus.
Fix: sing a known chorus, ask which line repeats most, student names it.
notes.prep: The craft word for today. Every slide from here uses it.

slides.title: The man and the bird
lines: Xavier Rudd is an Australian musician.
A red-tailed black cockatoo stopped him.
That bird is sacred to Aboriginal people.
He wrote the whole song that night.

notes.answer: open - the feeling was strong and he did not want to lose it
beats: POINT to the bird.
SAY: A red-tailed black cockatoo. Sacred to Aboriginal people in the Kimberley.
SAY: Rudd was up there when one stopped him in his tracks.
He wrote the whole song that same night, on the beach.
ASK: Why write it that same night, do you think?
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: the feeling was strong, he might lose it
trap: treating the bird as a pet or a cartoon.
Fix: say sacred means it carries meaning, student says the word back.
notes.prep: Context before the listen. Rudd has Aboriginal, Irish and Scottish heritage and was adopted by Yolngu people in 2003.
notes.sources: Xavier Rudd interviews and Wikipedia, checked September 2026. Song released 2012, runs 7 min 11 sec

slides.title: What the song stands up for
lines: Aboriginal people have been here 60,000 years.
From 1788 they were forced off their land.
Children were taken from their families.
Culture, language and Country are still here.

beats: SAY: Aboriginal people have been here more than sixty thousand years.
SAY: From 1788 they were forced off the land they belonged to.
Governments took children from their families for most of a century.
SAY: We call those children the Stolen Generations.
The national apology to them came in 2008, before you were born.
POINT to the last line.
SAY: Culture, language and Country are still here. That matters most.
trap: thinking this is all safely in the past.
Fix: name the Goodes film, ask if that felt long ago, student answers.
notes.care: some students may have family in this history. Quiet child -> quiet job.
notes.prep: Four facts, said plainly, ending on survival not despair. No spotlight on any student. Rudd's own great-grandmother had her child taken.

slides.title: How we listen
slides.label: Our agreement for the next seven minutes

beats: SAY: Seven minutes. The whole song, start to finish, no stopping.
SAY: It opens with singing and yidaki, the didgeridoo.
Some of it will not sound like English. That is not a joke.
SAY: If a part sounds strange to you, listen harder, not louder.
It is somebody's language and somebody's Country.
POINT to the three agreements.
SAY: Voices off. Follow the words. Right to the end.
PRESS PLAY. Stand at the back and watch faces, not the screen.
trap: a laugh at the opening singing.
Fix: pause it, one calm line - that is someone's language - restart from zero.
notes.prep: Respect is taught here, not assumed. Do this before you touch play. If a student asks what language it is, say honestly that we do not name what we cannot check.

slides.title: What stayed with you?
questions: One word: how did that song feel?
Which line stayed with you? Why that one?
Did any line come back more than once?

notes.answer: open - any feeling word, and any line they can point to on the sheet
beats: SAY: Do not talk yet. Sit with it for ten seconds.
ASK: One word for how that felt.
10 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: sad, strong, angry, calm, proud
ASK: Which line stayed with you?
30 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: a line they can point to on the sheet
CIRCULATE. Listen for a line that comes back. That is your I Do hook.
trap: talking over the last note of the song.
Fix: hand up for silence, ten seconds, then release the talk.
notes.prep: Protected response time after a heavy listen. Three minutes, then move on.

slides.title: Watch me find the line that repeats
slides.extract: [ The chorus goes here. Run scripts/inject_lyrics.py, or paste it from your lyric sheet. ]

notes.answer: the line that comes back after every verse - the refrain
beats: READ the chorus aloud once, slowly.
SAY: Watch me hunt for the line he will not drop.
POINT to the line that comes back.
SAY: There it is. And there again. That is the refrain.
SAY: Now I ask what that line wants from me.
MODEL: He repeats this line because he wants us to ...
trap: naming the loudest line, not the repeated one.
Fix: count how often each line appears, student names it.
notes.stretch: Find a second repeat: a word, a sound, an instrument.
notes.help: Highlight the chorus first, then count the repeats with a partner.
notes.prep: PASTE THE CHORUS into the extract box before you teach. Model: read, count repeats, name the ask.
notes.tag: [I Do | Explicit teaching | SC1, SC2 | HITS 3, 4]

slides.title: What does he want us to do?
slides.extract: [ Four lines of Verse 2 go here. Run scripts/inject_lyrics.py, or paste them yourself. ]

notes.answer: open - keep fighting for culture and land
beats: CHORAL READ the verse, together on three.
SAY: The chorus made us feel. Now he says what to do.
ASK: What does he want them to do?
40 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: keep fighting, keep going, do not give up
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: which word told you?
Less -> reread two lines, ask who he speaks to, re-ask.
trap: saying he wants us to feel sad.
Fix: point to the verbs, ask what they order, student rewrites.
notes.stretch: Who is he speaking to? Give your evidence.
notes.help: Underline every verb first, then answer.
notes.prep: Guided practice on new text, same craft move. SC2, seven minutes.

slides.title: Why does a songwriter repeat a line?
slides.prompt: Voices off. Fingers at your chest, then show me.

options.text: To fill up time in the song
To make sure you remember that idea
Because they ran out of new words

notes.answer: B - to make sure you remember that idea
beats: SAY: Three reasons. Only one is his real reason.
ASK: Why does a songwriter repeat a line?
15 sec. Cue: fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: B
SCAN fingers, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call one B: what do you remember?
Less -> say a jingle, ask why it stuck, re-ask.
REVEAL after fingers.
SAY: B. Repeat the line you want them to remember.
trap: choosing A because the song is long.
Fix: ask what they remember from the song, student re-answers.
notes.stretch: Name an advert line you cannot forget.
notes.help: Cover A and C. Ask only whether B is true.
notes.prep: The hinge before group writing. Under 80% means write one class refrain together first.

slides.title: Write the line they will remember
slides.task: Write one line you would repeat for people whose rights are ignored.
steps: Choose who you stand up for
Write the one line you repeat
Add two lines that show why
slides.frame: We stand up for ___ . Our line is ___ .

notes.answer: open - one short line that asks for something, not a nice slogan
beats: POINT to the task.
SAY: One line. The line your whole group would repeat.
SAY: Choose real people. Refugees, people with disability, kids left out.
Name yours before you write.
TIME 10 minutes. CIRCULATE. Ask each group to say their line aloud.
TIME 2 minutes to share. One group says their line, class repeats it.
trap: writing a whole verse and no repeated line.
Fix: ask which line they would say twice, the group circles it.
notes.stretch: Write a second line that answers the first.
notes.help: Give the frame filled to the first blank. The group writes only the line.
notes.prep: Independent application of SC3. Twelve minutes including the share. Steer groups off jokes early.
notes.tag: [You Do | Mastery and application | SC3 | HITS 5, 10]

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Write the line Xavier Rudd repeats. What does it make you feel?
Now write one thing the verse asks us to do.

notes.answer: the repeated line, a feeling word, and one thing the verse asks
beats: SAY: On your own now. Booklet open, lyric sheet beside it.
ASK: The repeated line, how it feels, one thing the verse asks.
180 sec. Cue: voices off, quick write in your own booklet.
EXPECT: the refrain, a feeling word, a keep-going answer
COLLECT booklets. RECORD who gave no feeling word for the small group.
trap: copying the line and stopping there.
Fix: none now, record the name and pick it up tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence. The line alone is SC1; the feeling and the ask are SC2.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner the one line from today you will still remember tomorrow.
takeaways: Repeat the line you want them to remember.
slides.notes: Read the three I can lines together. Thumbs on cue, then the turn and tell. Listen for a repeated line plus what it asks.
